settings.subtitle: Language, safety and maintenance options.
settings.restorePoint: Create a restore point before changes
settings.restorePoint.description: A system restore point is created once per session before the first tweak is applied. Requires administrator rights.
settings.revertAll.description: Restores the original values of every tweak this app has applied. Settings that were already in place are left untouched.
settings.revertAll.title: Revert changes

category.input.title: Input lag
category.input.subtitle: Timer, USB, PCIe and keyboard settings that add delay between your hand and the screen.
boost.subtitle: Fixes input lag while a game is running. Everything it changes is restored when the game closes.
boost.fix.nothing: Input tweaks are already in place  ·  Game Boost is on
boost.fix.done: Input lag fix applied  ·  {0} tweaks  ·  Game Boost is on
boost.fix.doneFailed: Input lag fix applied  ·  {0} tweaks, {1} failed  ·  Game Boost is on
boost.hint.off: Turn it on to improve input response in every game automatically.
boost.hint.waiting: It starts by itself when a game launches and stops when you close it.
boost.live.powerBlocked: CPU boost was refused by Windows
boost.master.description: Watches for running games and applies the options below only while one is running.
boost.timer.description: Windows checks timers and input about 64 times a second by default. This raises it to 2000 times a second while a game runs, which reduces micro stutter and input delay.
boost.timer.hint: Needs “Honor timer requests system-wide” on the Input lag page, then a restart. Otherwise Windows 11 ignores the request.
boost.priority.description: Raises the game to high priority and stops Windows from slowing it down in power saving mode.
boost.power.description: While plugged in, keeps all cores awake, the CPU at full speed and PCIe and USB from sleeping. Restored when the game closes.
boost.power.hint: Windows refused to change the power settings, so this option was skipped.
boost.games.description: Games installed through Steam, Epic, GOG, Riot, EA, Ubisoft, Rockstar and Xbox are found automatically. Add any other program by its process name.
settings.tray: Keep running in the tray when closed
settings.tray.description: Closing the window hides it to the tray so Game Boost keeps working. Only applies while Game Boost is on.
settings.startup.description: Starts minimized to the tray at sign in, with administrator rights. Requires administrator.
category.network.title: Network and ping
category.network.subtitle: Adapter, Wi-Fi and Windows settings that add delay or spikes to every packet. The distance to the game server stays the same, this removes what your own PC adds.
boost.wifi.description: Windows looks for other networks about once a minute, which shows up as a ping spike on Wi-Fi. Scanning is paused while a game runs and resumes when it closes. Until then Wi-Fi will not reconnect by itself if the signal drops.
boost.vibrance.description: Makes colors more saturated so player models stand out, only while CS2 is running. Your usual colors return when the game closes. Works on screens driven by NVIDIA and AMD graphics.
boost.vibrance.unsupported: NO SUPPORTED NVIDIA OR AMD SCREEN FOUND
ping.title: Ping test
ping.description: Measures the delay to your router and to the internet, with jitter and packet loss. Spikes at the router come from your own connection, not from the game server.
ping.advice.wifiUnstable: Wi-Fi itself is adding delay and spikes. A network cable is the biggest single ping fix. Otherwise move closer to the router or use the 5 GHz band.
ping.advice.localUnstable: The local network is unstable: something is loading the router, such as downloads, streams or other devices.
ping.advice.wifi: Wi-Fi is stable right now, but it can still spike under load. A cable gives the lowest and steadiest ping.
ping.advice.good: Your local connection is clean. In-game ping now depends on the distance to the game server.
